root_cause.text: In the mm swap/migration path, do_swap_page() used a non-blocking folio_trylock() on device-private folios and, on failure, let hmm_range_fault() repeatedly retry without waiting, causing CPU-spinning that could starve the lock holder’s required work item and create a livelock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “If hmm_range_fault() fails a folio_trylock() in do_swap_page ... the function will spin until it succeeds,” and the fix changes do_swap_page() from immediately unlocking the PTE lock to calling softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, vmf->ptl), i.e. waiting for the migration/device-private entry to be unlocked instead of spinning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename migration_entry_wait_on_locked() to softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked() to align the interface with softleaf terminology without changing its signature.
intent_record.what: The declaration of the function was renamed from "migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)" to "softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl)", with the parameter list and __releases(ptl) annotation unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this does not directly change behavior in this header diff, but it changes the exported symbol/interface name that callers must use, likely aligning the API with a broader softleaf-based abstraction rather than a migration-specific one.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a non-MIGRATION stub for softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked() that warns once and unlocks the spinlock to provide safe fallback behavior.
intent_record.what: A new static inline stub function named softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_t entry, spinlock_t *ptl) was added under the CONFIG_MIGRATION-disabled section, annotated with __releases(ptl), and implemented to call WARN_ON_ONCE(1) followed by spin_unlock(ptl).
intent_record.how: When CONFIG_MIGRATION is not enabled, any code path that invokes this function now links against a fallback implementation that emits a one-time warning and releases the provided page-table lock instead of lacking the symbol or leaving the lock held.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the function documentation to reflect that the helper applies to both migration and device_private entries, not just migration entries.
intent_record.what: The diff only changes the kernel-doc comment for the function: it renames the documented symbol from "migration_entry_wait_on_locked" to "softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked", broadens the description from handling only migration entries to handling both migration and device_private entries, updates the @entry parameter description accordingly, and revises the explanatory text to mention device_private pages and refer more generally to holding the ptl for @entry.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it updates documentation so the comment matches a function intended to wait on either migration or device_private swap entries, improving API clarity and reducing misunderstanding by developers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename migration_entry_wait_on_locked to softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked to align the API with softleaf entry terminology without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The function definition name was changed from "migration_entry_wait_on_locked" to "softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked" while keeping the same parameters, return type, annotations, and body.
intent_record.how: At runtime behavior inside the function remains unchanged, but callers must now use the new symbol name, indicating the API is being generalized or renamed to operate on softleaf entries rather than specifically migration entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document that removing a device-private entry when dropping the last page reference also requires holding the page-table lock.
intent_record.what: Three comment lines were added to the block comment in migration_entry_wait_on_locked(), stating that any path dropping the last reference to a device-private page must acquire the page-table lock to remove the device-private entry.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it documents an additional locking and lifetime guarantee for device-private page entries, clarifying the synchronization assumptions around page validity while the page-table lock is held.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix do_swap_page() to wait correctly on locked softleaf swap entries instead of simply unmapping and unlocking the PTE.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a single call to pte_unmap_unlock(vmf->pte, vmf->ptl) with two separate calls: pte_unmap(vmf->pte) followed by softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, vmf->ptl) in the else branch of do_swap_page().
intent_record.how: Instead of immediately unmapping the PTE and unlocking the page-table lock, the code now unmaps the PTE and then waits on a locked softleaf entry while passing the existing lock context. This changes runtime behavior so that handling of this swap entry follows a synchronization path specific to locked softleaf entries, avoiding premature plain unlock behavior and ensuring proper waiting semantics before proceeding.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the softleaf-specific locked wait helper in migration_entry_wait() so softleaf migration entries are handled by the correct wait path.
intent_record.what: The call inside migration_entry_wait() was changed from migration_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl) to softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl) when softleaf_is_migration(entry) is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now waits on the softleaf-specific locked entry handler instead of the migration-specific one for entries identified as softleaf migration entries, ensuring the wait path matches the entry type being checked.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update `migration_entry_wait_huge()` to call the correct locked-entry wait helper and fix the accompanying comment reference.
intent_record.what: The diff updates a comment to replace the referenced function name `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` with `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`, and changes the actual function call from `migration_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl)` to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes the code path in `migration_entry_wait_huge()` to invoke `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` instead of `migration_entry_wait_on_locked()` after releasing the hugetlb VMA read lock, aligning behavior with the renamed or intended helper function for waiting on the locked entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the softleaf-specific locked wait helper for PMD migration entries to correctly wait on the softleaf entry type.
intent_record.what: The function call inside pmd_migration_entry_wait() was changed from migration_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_from_pmd(*pmd), ptl) to softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(softleaf_from_pmd(*pmd), ptl), with the arguments and surrounding control flow left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the PMD still contains a migration entry, the code now waits using the softleaf-specific locked wait helper instead of the generic migration-entry helper, aligning the wait operation with the softleaf entry type produced by softleaf_from_pmd(*pmd) and correcting the handling of that entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the softleaf-specific wait helper for softleaf migration entries in huge PMD migration handling.
intent_record.what: The code replaces the call to migration_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl) with softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(entry, ptl) inside the softleaf_is_migration(entry) conditional in migrate_vma_collect_huge_pmd().
intent_record.how: At runtime, when a softleaf migration entry is encountered, the function now waits using the softleaf-specific wait helper instead of the generic migration wait helper before unlocking and returning -EAGAIN, ensuring the wait behavior matches the entry type being handled.

consistency_review.core_intent: Rename migration_entry_wait_on_locked to softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked to align the API with softleaf entry terminology without changing behavior.
Fix memory-management wait paths to use the softleaf-specific locked-entry helpers for softleaf migration and swap entries, including huge/PMD migration handling and safe fallback support.

relevance_review.reason: The change is only an API/function rename for terminology alignment and explicitly does not alter behavior. The vulnerability is about busy-retry/livelock in do_swap_page()/hmm_range_fault() due to non-blocking folio_trylock() handling, which this rename does not address.

The root cause is incorrect non-blocking handling in the swap/migration fault path that fails to wait on locked entries, leading to retry spinning. This group explicitly changes do_swap_page() and migration wait paths to use the correct softleaf locked-entry wait helpers for swap and migration entries, directly addressing the missing/incorrect waiting behavior behind the livelock.

This change only updates documentation wording about the helper covering both migration and device_private entries. It does not modify the locking/retry behavior in do_swap_page() or hmm_range_fault() that caused the CPU-spinning livelock.

This change only documents page-table lock requirements when removing a device-private entry on last page reference drop. The vulnerability is caused by do_swap_page() using folio_trylock() and retrying without waiting, leading to CPU-spinning/livelock in hmm_range_fault(); documenting ptlock requirements does not address that retry/locking behavior.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix fallback in do_swap_page() for the relevant softleaf/device-private swap case. Instead of waiting on the locked entry, it simply drops the PTE lock and returns, enabling repeated hmm_range_fault() retries with no blocking and thus CPU-spinning/livelock.

The fix intent says this helper was wrong for softleaf migration entries and needed replacement by a softleaf-specific locked wait helper. Using the generic migration wait path on softleaf entries is directly tied to the incorrect non-wait/retry behavior in the swap/migration path.

Same underlying bug in huge-page migration wait handling: the generic locked migration wait helper was used where a softleaf-specific helper was required, contributing to incorrect handling of locked softleaf entries.
This PMD migration path likewise used the wrong locked-entry wait helper for a softleaf-derived entry. It reflects the same root cause of not using the proper softleaf-aware waiting path.

Device migration handling also used the generic migration wait helper for a softleaf migration entry. Since the vulnerability concerns device-private folios in swap/migration handling, this is a strong candidate for the flawed wait behavior.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix fallback in do_swap_page() drops the PTE lock and returns instead of waiting on the locked softleaf/device-private entry. That directly matches the root cause: hmm_range_fault() can immediately retry, causing a busy retry loop and potential livelock.

This uses the generic locked migration wait helper for a softleaf migration entry. The fix rationale indicates softleaf entries required a different wait helper, so this statement contributes to the incorrect wait behavior in the swap/migration path.
This PMD migration path similarly waits using the wrong helper for a softleaf-derived entry. That matches the root cause of not correctly blocking on locked softleaf/device-private entries.

This device migration path also uses the generic locked migration wait helper for a softleaf migration entry. Because the vulnerability involves device-private folios, this statement is part of the flawed waiting behavior.

commit 1afaeb8293c9addbf4f9140bdd22635fed763459
Author: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 5 17:26:28 2025 -0800

    mm/migrate: Trylock device page in do_swap_page
    
    Avoid multiple CPU page faults to the same device page racing by trying
    to lock the page in do_swap_page before taking an extra reference to the
    page. This prevents scenarios where multiple CPU page faults each take

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact device-private swap fault handling in do_swap_page(). The root cause is use of a non-blocking trylock on the device-private page, which on failure returns without waiting and allows repeated fault retries/spinning. That behavior is present here: `if (trylock_page(vmf->page)) { ... ret = vmf->page->pgmap->ops->migrate_to_ram(vmf); unlock_page(vmf->page); put_page(vmf->page); } else { pte_unmap_unlock(vmf->pte, vmf->ptl); }`. In the failure path of `trylock_page(vmf->page)`, the code only does `pte_unmap_unlock(vmf->pte, vmf->ptl);` and does not block on the page lock or otherwise wait for migration completion. This matches the vulnerable construct described: non-blocking lock attempt on a device-private folio/page with immediate retry behavior that can lead to CPU spinning/livelock. Therefore the buggy construct is present, and the fix is not present because the code still uses `trylock_page()` instead of waiting/locking behavior that would prevent repeated busy retries.
